pretrained video model. single-view human video can be incorporated similarly. video-only supervision can still improve understanding of task execution. adding video supervision opens up many forms of co-training. dreamzero’s future development will mainly emphasize more diverse scenes and objects, helping map its general video-prediction and planning capability correctly into actions. dreamdojo has different requirements. its core function is to simulate the future consequences of actions: it is an action-conditioned world model. such a model needs diverse actions as well as diverse objects and scenes. to improve dreamdojo, we would ideally make the action distribution as broad and even—and actions as unpredictable—as possible. a simulator’s goal is not to learn an excellent policy; it is to faithfully simulate world changes under varied actions. it can therefore use successful demonstrations, failures and even random trajectories. any data that help explain the consequences of different actions are valuable. training dreamdojo therefore requires increasing action diversity alongside object and scene diversity. in other words, the more uniform and irregular the action distribution is, the better the world model’s controllability. better controllability means more accurate feedback when simulating different actions, which in turn helps optimize policies afterward. this is the relationship i am describing. this raises a concern: would covering so many actions require a much larger dataset—perhaps 100 times larger? that concern is real, but the intended use matters. for policy optimization or test-time search, dreamdojo need not cover the entire action distribution perfectly. accurately simulating actions the policy is likely to produce can already make it useful. in practice, both models could start from the same dataset, such as one dominated by expert demonstrations. for dreamdojo, however, we would additionally prefer a more even action distribution, improving its modeling of different action outcomes. dreamzero serves as a policy; dreamdojo is a world model and simulator. together, they can form a model-based training framework. given a state, dreamzero samples a series of actions. dreamdojo simulates their future consequences. you can assign rewards to trajectories based on the resulting state evolution, then use those rewards to optimize dreamzero toward better actions. dreamdojo itself can also improve. once dreamzero—or another sufficiently mature policy—has reached a suitable level, you can deploy it in a real environment and collect actual state–action–transition data. updating dreamdojo with these data improves its modeling and simulation quality. in other words, dreamdojo can help optimize dreamzero, while real-world data continually improve dreamdojo itself. references shenyuan gao’s profile: https://github.com/little-podi dreamdojo: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06949 dreamzero: robotics，依然延续了过去在硬件设备、传感器和算法等方面的技术积累，把这些能力应用到一个新的方向——也就是具身智能与机器人领域。我们希望用“人的动作数字化”“高精度追踪”“动作捕捉”等核心技术，为这一新兴行业提供数据和技术支持。 的两个控制器、一个头显和两只脚部追踪器。恰巧在同一天，我们也看到了西湖机器人发布的项目（此处也可以给出建明访谈索引），使用的也是我们的全身动作捕捉系统pns。当时的视频里看到的效果非常震撼，迮炎杰甚至笑着说，压力有点大，要把自己的项目做得更好一点再发布。他也已经拿到了一整套我们的全身动捕设备，正在尝试用全身动作捕捉系统进行实时操作的研究。 这两天全网引发讨论的小鹏的发布我们也是亲历者。从 2023 年底开始，我们的技术团队就与小鹏人形机器人团队密集合作。这个团队的能力非常强，无论是本体制造、运动控制、大模型、多模态模型的探索，还是产品化能力，都是国内一线水准。他们使用了我们提供的数据和设备支持。 这次他们展示的女性机器人“完美步态”，所使用的数据就是通过我们的动作捕捉设备采集的，用于模仿学习，强化学习，模型训练。更多的细节因为保密协议不便透露。 同样也是前两天宇树发布的“身外化身”项目和几周前西湖机器人发布的实时遥操作中，视频里那位操控机器人的工程师身上穿戴的也是我们的惯性动作捕捉设备，这款设备名为 perception neuron studio，是目前全球销量最高的动捕设备。这套设备全身共有 17 个传感器：下半身 7 个，上半身 10 个；加上手套后再增加 10 个，一共 27 个 imu 传感器。这 27 个 imu 传感器可以采集原始的陀螺仪、磁力计和加速度计信息，并以 480 帧每秒的频率进行计算，得到身体各部位的相对位置和绝对姿态。 这些数据会被传入 axis studio 软件中，软件会进一步进行三层计算。第一层是前向动力学（forward kinematics），保证整体姿态成型；第二层是逆向动力学（inverse kinematics），保证末端位置和脚步触地稳定且符合物理规律；第三层是基于物理引擎的约束层，用更多的物理定律与人体构型规律作为最优化算法的边界条件。 人体有很多约束条件。为了研究人的动作如何数字化，我们花了很多时间研究了人体动力学结构甚至解剖过大体老师，比如肘关节反向弯曲容差很小，手指的第二指节是单自由度，第一指节是双自由度，前臂由于尺骨挠骨具备自旋能力等。还有一些物理约束，比如重力、地面接触、摩擦、冲击、跳跃时的势能转换等。通过这几层计算，可以把原始的 imu 数据转化为人体动作姿态的数字化序列。而这整个把人的动作数字化的过程就是动作捕捉。 前面提到的几个研究工作，都使用了不同的动作捕捉技术和模型训练方式，最终实现了完美步态（小鹏）、实时全身遥操作（宇树/西湖/twist1）、基于稀疏追踪传感的遥操作（twist2）等成果。我们与这些科研工作者的交流也非常密切，经常会互相交换行业和学术方面的信息。 动作捕捉（motion capture）指的是将人的动作和姿态数字化的过程。这个定义本身与使用的方式和方法无关。无论是通过计算机视觉、传感器、磁追踪，还是外骨骼等不同技术手段，只要能把人的动作姿态捕获下来、转化为数字序列，都属于动作捕捉。 动作捕捉这一技术的应用历史非常悠久。早在 20 世纪 70 年代，英国一家名为 vicon 的公司就已经开始从事光学动作捕捉研究。vicon是英国的上市企业，也是该领域的先驱与标杆，至今仍被认为是光学动捕质量的天花板。50年前vicon的第一代系统需要借助巨大体积的摄像机，只能追踪极少量的标记点（marker）。 后来真正让动作捕捉被普罗大众广泛认识并进入主流生产流程的，是詹姆斯·卡梅隆（james cameron）导演的《阿凡达》第一部。影片拍摄过程中，团队为实现实时可视化和实时渲染，建立了一整套虚拟拍摄（virtual production）的生产管线。这个项目的成功不仅赢得了多项奥斯卡奖，也催生了多家业内知名的特效流程技术服务公司。 诺亦腾科技成立于 2012 年，并在 2014 年推出第一代产品。当时采用了极具突破性的定价策略，将行业价格降低了两个数量级。原本需要上百万元才能完成的动捕工作，几万元人民币就能实现，因此迅速吸引了全球大量用户。 我们的设备被广泛应用于多个领域。例如，《权力的游戏》第五季开始，剧中“异鬼”等群体角色的动作捕捉都使用了我们的设备，当时片场配备了十余套系统，由七八位特技演员完成全部动作采集；《金刚狼》《星际迷航》《星球大战》等影视项目的特效制作中也都有我们的设备参与。 在体育运动领域，像高尔夫球手泰格·伍兹（tiger woods）和麦克罗伊（rory mcilroy）等，他们的教练团队长期使用我们的动捕设备分析体态、挥杆动作的动力链。中国的多位奥运冠军以及现代五项国家队，也在日常训练中使用我们的系统进行数字化分析。 此外，我们的动捕技术还应用于虚拟现实、游戏和交互设备中。包括oculus、htc、索尼 playstation vr 等多家公司，在手部追踪、数字手套、vr 交互等环节都使用了我们的技术授权，技术服务或配件。 到了 2023 年底，我们发现一个新的增长点来自机器人领域。这促使我个人开始重新关注机器人行业，并创立了noitom robotics 公司，专门面向机器人领域提供服务，与科研团队和机器人本体厂商展开广泛合作。回过头来看，过去十几年的积累似乎正是为这一刻做准备——把人的动作捕捉与机器人的智能控制结合起来，这是一件非常有意义的事情，也让我感到非常幸运。 动作捕捉（motion capture）指的是把人的动作和姿态数字化的过程。它并不限定于某一种方式或技术手段，可以通过计算机视觉、传感器、磁追踪、外骨骼等多种方式实现。核心在于将人的姿态和动作固化、捕捉，并转换成数字序列。 光学动作捕捉（optical motion capture）长期以来被认为是科研领域的“金标准”（goldstandard），因为它具备绝对精度。光学动捕的原理是利用多台高速工业相机，在 850–950 纳米的红外波段下进行全局快门曝光，所有像素点同时曝光，不会出现卷帘式逐行曝光的问题，因此同步性极高。优质的光学相机每秒可采集 1200 帧（fps），常规系统的帧率一般在 120–240 fps 之间。 在一个 15 平方米左右的房间内，通常每平方米需要一到两台相机才能实现完整覆盖。如果要实现专业级的全身捕捉，例如在好莱坞电影制作中，15 平方米的空间可能需要安装 20–30 台相机。较大的空间，如 100 平方米，即便是稀疏布设也需要约 40–50 台相机（好几万甚至十几万一台）。高品质光学动捕的定位精度可达到亚毫米级，多个标记点组成的刚体姿态定位精度能达到 0.05 度，因此它被科研人员视为精度意义上的金标准。 然而，光学动捕系统需要复杂的安装环境和高成本的设备。相机价格昂贵，搭建一个完整系统往往需要四五十万元人民币。相比之下，惯性动作捕捉（inertial motion capture）在环境适应性和使用便捷性上具有明显优势。惯性动捕无需任何外部设施，可在室内外任意环境中使用，只需穿戴设备并做几次校准即可开始采集，成本也远低于光学系统。 惯性动捕的缺点在于缺乏绝对精度。它依赖穿戴传感器对角速度、加速度和磁场的积分计算位置与姿态，因此存在累积误差（drift），精度一般为厘米级，属于相对精度。不同厂商通过算法优化可延缓漂移的出现，但整体而言，惯性动捕无法提供光学动捕那样的绝对准确性。 在机器人领域，如果需要高精度的“真值”（ground truth）级别数据，如捕捉人体或物体在空间中的绝对位置，通常会选择光学动捕；而在遥操作（teleoperation）等需要环境适应灵活性、易用性和实时响应的场景中，则更常采用惯性动捕。 目前更先进的方案是光学与惯性的混合系统（hybrid tracking）。这种融合方式结合了光学系统的高精度和惯性系统的连续性，能够在遮挡环境下保持数据稳定。例如，当一只手遮挡另一只手时，光学系统会丢失标记点信息，而惯性系统仍能提供连续数据，通过融合计算，可以同时保证数据的精度与连续性。 除了光学和惯性技术，外骨骼也是一种早期出现的动作捕捉形式。早在 20 世纪 70 年代末至 80 年代初，一些相关研究机构就使用带有编码器的外骨骼结构进行人体动作追踪。随着机器人研究的兴起，越来越多研究者重新采用外骨骼式设备进行遥操作或动作捕捉，这一做法延续了早期的思路。 此外，还有基于磁场的动作捕捉方式。例如部分厂商使用高频弱磁场与三轴线圈，来判断传感器在空间中的位置和姿态，应用于数据手套和控制器的追踪。这类技术曾被美国空军及其他工业领域采用，后续也被雷蛇（razer）等公司用于消费级产品。 总体而言，从 20 世纪 70 年代到今天，动作捕捉技术经历了半个多世纪的发展。从最初的科研实验装置，到电影工业、体育分析、虚拟现实，再到如今的机器人与具身智能领域，动作捕捉持续演进，成为连接人类动作与数字世界的重要技术。 5. 机器人应用领域里不同动捕方案如何选择 如果站在一个更系统的角度去看，首先要区分清楚动捕数据最终指向的目标是什么——是追求“视觉合理性”，还是追求“任务成功率与操作精度”。 如果目标是视觉合理性，那么从视频中提取的数据其实是可以用的。例如我熟悉的青年学者曾爱玲曾经制作过一个非常大的数据集（链接见references部分），从互联网上收集了海量视频，这类数据在视觉层面上的质量完全够用。因为此类视频数据的关键点，在相机视角上的投影通常是准确的。但问题在于它缺乏深度信息。单目视频难以保证纵深方向的精度；只有当使用双目相机且基线较大时，才能得到一些深度参考。 如果训练的目的是让模型输出或机器人的最终表现“看起来像那么回事”，例如让机器人学会跳舞、打拳，与人类视频示范的视觉效果相似，那么即使是单目视频提取出的动作数据也能满足需求。这种模型的目标只是让机器人在视频视角下的动作与人类看起来一致，是一种较为轻量的应用。 但如果目标是实现高动态动作，并要求物理合理性，让机器人能够站稳、跳跃，行动路径回环，甚至进行交互行为，那么对空间精度就有了很高要求。这类任务，比如宇树的身外化身和迮炎杰的twist系列（链接见references部分）工作，他们都将自己的平台定义为人形机器人遥操作平台，用于采集真实交互数据。这种情况下，数据采集必须具备空间精度，需要更专业的动捕设备来支持。 在选择专业设备时，会根据使用环境和目标需求再细分两种情况。 如果是实验室（in-lab）或工厂（in-factory）环境，空间可控、预算相对充裕，并且对精度要求极高，例如需要双手协同的动作采集，这时推荐使用光学动作捕捉系统。光学系统适合室内搭建，精度高、同步性好，是科研和高质量数据采集的理想选择。例如亚马逊机器人实验室这样的机构，要构建高精度实验系统，就应使用光学或光学与惯性混合系统。 但如果是在非固定环境，比如户外或临时场景下，希望能快速部署、成本较低且操作灵活，那么惯性动作捕捉系统是更合适的选择。如果是在户外或普通环境中实现遥操作，这类需求就非常适合使用惯性动捕。 不同场景、不同需求下，最优方案会完全不同。每种动作捕捉技术——光学、惯性、磁追踪、外骨骼等——都有其存在的合理性。正因如此，这些方式至今仍被使用并不断发展。选择哪种系统，往往需要根据场景和环境逐一分析、权衡，这是一项必须具体情况具体判断的工作。 我觉得首先并不一定要选择诺亦腾的数据或设备，我非常乐意与大家交流，并提供一些公允的建议，再由各方自行做出选择。整个行业目前仍处在非常早期的阶段，我们希望能有更多的人共同参与，一起解决数据的问题。当前最大的瓶颈，毫无疑问是数据。大模型时代，语言模型不缺数据，可以全网爬取语料；自动驾驶厂商也能通过大量实车采集积累数据。但在机器人领域，这样的规模尚未实现。 从整体来看，现实世界中的数据可以分为几类，而这些类型的数据最终都是行业的刚需，必须协同结合，才能在体量和质量上达到足够的覆盖度。 首先是真机遥操作数据，它极为重要。其他类型的数据，例如人本数据或合成数据，都无法体现机器人的本体特性。只有真机数据才能包含机器人的传感、驱动、构型等真实特征，也反映不同型号在生产制造中的差异性。虽然真机数据的获取昂贵，灵活性不足，也难以跨本体使用，但每一款机器人都必须具备至少数千小时的真机遥操作数据。就像汽车行业，每推出一款新车型，都要重新采集大规模的路测数据一样，机器人在构型或硬件特性变化时，也必须重新采集数据。 因此，真机遥操作数据是不可或缺的，但由于成本与效率问题，规模难以做到很大。这类数据更多承担本体特性对齐作用，而非学习技能的主要来源。技能与规则的学习，应当依赖其他类型的数据。 近几年，越来越多的研究者和公司将关注点转向以人为中心的数据采集。人本数据通过直接记录人的交互行为和视觉信息，为机器人提供丰富的模仿和理解样本。这类数据类似于ego4d、egodex、egopressure、project aria/aria2 等项目中的视觉为主的交互数据集。 不过，人本（human centric）数据的定义存在分歧。部分研究者主张应在自然环境（in the wild）中采集，确保数据足够自由、足够多样。但要做到真正的 in the wild，必须在模态、维度和精度上做出牺牲。如果采集系统复杂、穿戴负担重，就无法进入家庭、工厂、老人院等真实环境中。也有研究团队希望“既要又要”，既追求大规模体量，又追求高模态与高精度，结果往往陷入矛盾。 因此，即便是人本数据这个数据门类里，可能也需要进一步分层。上层是高精度、多模态的相对小规模数据，约十万至百万小时级别，用于建立高质量、全模态、全维度的基准；下层是更大体量的 in the wild 数据，降低穿戴复杂度和精度要求，追求更广泛的场景覆盖。 在此之下，还有一层非常关键的合成数据与互联网数据。这类数据能为真机与人本数据提供大规模增强（data augmentation），通过仿真与合成环境扩展轨迹、目标、背景与策略的多样性，从而把数据体量放大数百倍。自动驾驶早期就广泛使用这种方式，对真实数据进行模拟扩展，以覆盖极端情况。 总体来看，我并不以自身设备或数据集为出发点去思考问题，而是希望行业能真正联手解决数据瓶颈。如果大家无法共同构建起完整的数据体系，这个行业的发展将停滞不前。我们需要更大规模、更高层次的数据驱动，才能推动机器人智能真正向前。 诺亦腾机器人并不是一个单纯的设备厂商，或者说，并不希望仅仅成为设备厂商。虽然诺亦腾科技（noitom）在很多层面上可以被视为设备制造企业，但诺亦腾机器人（noitom robotics）不同。诺亦腾机器人希望通过多种方式去解决行业中的数据问题。诺亦腾机器人既可以是服务提供方，也可以是数据集的授权方。 未来很长一段时间，我会用设备去“交朋友”，而不是通过卖设备赚钱。对于很多学者，我会直接免费提供设备；对于一些优秀的行业合作伙伴，也基本以成本价、甚至半买半送的形式让他们使用。目的是让更多的人能用上这项技术，推动研究与应用的发展。 我会投入大量精力和资本建设自己的数据工厂，积累十万小时、甚至百万小时级别的数据集。我们积累这些数据的核心目的，是为了帮助整个行业降低成本。听起来似乎有些矛盾——为什么一个第三方数据厂商去采集数据，反而能让行业更便宜？但我的逻辑是，只有那些能够跨本体、可复用的大规模数据，才值得积累。 我们会用一些巧妙的办法将采集到的人本数据集（human-centric dataset）对齐到合作伙伴或客户不同的机器人本体构型上，并向他们授权使用。因为这些数据具备跨本体映射能力，可以多次授权、重复使用，这样做能显著降低全行业在数据建设上的重复投入和浪费。 举个例子，我们最近与一家大型企业达成了千万级规模的数据授权合作。在这份协议中，我们授权的数据价格甚至略低于采集成本。但我也花了很长时间去说服这家企业放弃数据的完全独占权，通过这种商业模式，可以让行业内的数据积累更具效率和可持续性。 我认为，这就是我们能够为行业带来的最大价值。我们需要合理的营收，以维持数十人到上百人的研发团队持续运作，不断进行技术投入。同时，通过积累可重复授权的数据集，让整个行业都能以远低于自身采集成本的代价，获得高质量的数据资源。 这也是我的愿景。能否做到，还需要时间去实践。未来两三年，我都会专注在这件事情上。如果有机器人本体厂商、模型公司或投资人对这个方向感兴趣，欢迎与我交流，我们一定能找到合适的合作方式。 我们目前最需要的，是人才。现在最紧急在招的有三类岗位。 第一类是产品经理和项目经理（product manager / project manager）。我们在数据和机器人领域都非常缺人，无论年轻还是资深，只要有志于这个方向的都非常欢迎。 第二类是算法相关的人才。我们的首席科学家韩磊博士正在积极招募在多模态模型、vla、强化学习以及数据科学等方向有经验的研究人员。无论是年轻学者、实习生还是全职的研究科学家（research scientist），我们都有空缺岗位，希望能够吸引更多真正热爱机器人算法与模型研究的伙伴加入。 第三类是传感器与硬件相关的岗位。过去我们在硬件领域确实有一定积累，但这只是一个起点。现在市面上大多数用于数据采集的动作捕捉和追踪设备，其实都是为影视特效或游戏行业设计的，而不是为机器人数据采集而开发的。然而，机器人数据采集的市场远远大于影视行业，对设备的需求也更高。这一领域需要专门为不同环境——无论是 in the wild、in the factory 还是 research lab——设计的新型硬件。 我们正在积极推动这一方向，因此特别需要硬件规划与传感器相关的人才。例如磁定位传感器专家、imu 专家、光学传感器专家、算法工程化专家、固件工程师、bsp（板级支持包）工程师等。如果你在这些方向有经验，或者想在更具潜力的赛道找到新的机会，欢迎加入我们。 如果贵公司有明确的边界，希望将数据采集、数据集制备等非核心但关键的环节交给专业团队来负责，我们会非常乐意合作。我们能以最合理的价格、最充足的热情和最专业的水准，帮助你们高效完成工作。 ref： twist系列： https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.02833 https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02832 曾爱玲数据集： business. as embodied intelligence entered 2025, certain concepts attracted renewed attention: world models, for example, which we discussed in depth in our 2023 and 2024 interviews—robot data, dynamics for general manipulation—and umi, covered in robot data, episode 2: cheng chi and zhenjia xu on umi, a physical api for robot training. previously fashionable concepts, such as vla and teleoperation with matched embodiments, were sometimes pushed aside in these comparisons. investment in china's embodied-intelligence sector seemed to have become investment in labels. investors busily searched for projects carrying a particular conceptual tag, while startups busily attached new tags to themselves. this concept-driven investing closely resembles the earlier copy to china model. when an overseas company reveals a technical direction, investors rush to find a domestic equivalent. it has also prompted many outstanding chinese researchers in the united states to found their companies in deep secrecy, fearing that peers in china will copy their work. the real contribution of embodied intelligence is not the valuations inflated by successive waves of fashionable concepts. writing in 2025, as a robotics investor a little fatigued by the repetition, i am pleasantly surprised that some domestic entrepreneurs still dare to lead rather than follow. the human data series aims to draw attention to a data route that has not yet been overexposed but may hold tremendous potential. i also hope readers notice people willing to take responsibility for creating value and moving the industry forward, rather than following trends merely to raise money. for the final interview in the human data series, i am honored to speak with ruoli dai, founder of noitom robotics. research projects relate to noitom robotics 3. an introduction to motion capture 4. differences between motion-capture approaches 5. choosing a motion-capture system for robotics 6. why choose noitom robotics' equipment and data? 7. near-term contributions to the community 8. talent needs 9. business partnerships i am ruoli dai, founder and chief executive officer of noitom robotics. we focus on applying motion capture, high-precision tracking and computer vision to support the entire robotics data pipeline. our work covers collection equipment, data-collection services, post-processing, annotation and licensing our own datasets. we aim to provide complete data infrastructure and technical support for the robotics industry. we founded noitom robotics in 2025. before that, i founded a motion-capture equipment company called noitom. the name is the word motion spelled backward. its core technologies and products revolve around one goal: digitizing human movement. we have long studied how wearable sensors and computer vision can precisely capture and reconstruct human motion digitally. over more than a decade—thirteen years, to be precise—we served industries and customers around the world, including film visual effects, virtual reality, human–computer interaction, sports analysis and healthcare. in the relatively specialized inertial motion-capture market, we became a global leader, with a market share exceeding 70% by our estimate. my new company, noitom robotics, carries forward our experience in hardware, sensors and algorithms, applying it to embodied intelligence and robotics. we want to use our capabilities in digitizing human motion, high-precision tracking and motion capture to support this emerging industry with data and technology. there is a natural logic behind this direction. humanoid robots and embodied-intelligence systems depend heavily on digitized human interaction, behavior and poses. they need to learn skills and capabilities from those digital records. that underlying logic creates a new opportunity for us and brings me back to robotics. my phd research concerned active vibration damping and grasp control in robotics. returning to the field fifteen or sixteen years after graduating feels both like a continuation and a homecoming. yanjie ze's first twist project—see human data, episode 1—mocap: twist—uses optical tracking, probably optitrack if my understanding is correct. when i met him at stanford about a month before this interview, i saw early demonstrations of twist2. he was using two pico controllers, a headset and two foot trackers. coincidentally, that same day we saw a project released by westlake robotics that used our full-body pns motion-capture system. the video was striking. yanjie joked that he felt some pressure and wanted to improve his project before releasing it. he had also received a complete set of our whole-body capture equipment and was experimenting with using it for real-time operation. the original transcript suggests adding an interview index here, but provides no specific link. we also witnessed the xpeng launch that had generated online discussion in the days before this interview. since late 2023, our technical team had worked closely with xpeng's humanoid-robot team. it is a very capable team, among china's leading groups in hardware manufacturing, motion control, large models, multimodal-model exploration and product development. they used our data and equipment support. the data behind the female humanoid’s “perfect gait” in that demonstration was collected with our motion-capture equipment and used for imitation learning, reinforcement learning and model training. confidentiality agreements prevent me from sharing further details. the engineer operating the robot in unitree’s recent “out-of-body avatar” teleoperation demonstration and westlake robotics' demonstration a few weeks earlier was also wearing our inertial capture equipment. it is called perception neuron studio, which we describe as the world's best-selling motion-capture system. it has seventeen body sensors: seven for the lower body and ten for the upper body. the gloves add ten more, for twenty-seven imus in total. these sensors collect raw gyroscope, magnetometer and accelerometer information. processing at 480 frames per second yields relative positions and absolute orientations for the body segments. this data enters axis studio, which performs three layers of computation. the first is forward kinematics, establishing the overall body configuration. the second is inverse kinematics, helping maintain stable end-effector positions and foot contacts consistent with physical constraints. the third is a physics-engine-based constraint layer, using physical laws and anatomical structure as boundary conditions for optimization. editorial correction: the chinese transcript calls the first two layers forward and inverse dynamics, but gives the english terms forward kinematics and inverse kinematics; those kinematic terms are used here. the human body has many constraints. we spent considerable time studying its mechanical structure to understand how to digitize movement, even studying anatomy through donated cadavers. the elbow has little tolerance for bending backward; the second finger joint has one degree of freedom, while the first has two; and the radius and ulna allow the forearm to rotate about its axis. physical constraints include gravity, ground contact, friction, impacts and potential-energy conversion during a jump. these layers of computation transform raw imu data into digital sequences of human poses. that entire process of digitizing human movement is motion capture. the projects mentioned earlier use different capture technologies and training methods to achieve results such as xpeng’s “perfect gait”, real-time whole-body teleoperation from unitree, westlake robotics and twist, and sparse-tracking-based teleoperation in twist2. we communicate closely with these researchers and frequently exchange industry and academic information. motion capture means digitizing human movements and poses. the definition does not prescribe a specific method. computer vision, sensors, magnetic tracking and exoskeletons can all be used. if a method captures human movement and turns it into a digital sequence, it is motion capture. the technology has a long history. the interview traces vicon's optical motion-capture lineage back to the 1970s. the british company is a pioneer and benchmark in the field, and i still regard it as setting the standard for optical-capture quality. its first-generation systems, described in the interview as dating back roughly fifty years, used enormous cameras and tracked only a few markers. editorial clarification: vicon's official history dates its first product to 1979 and the start of trading to 1984. vicon is the motion-capture business of the publicly listed oxford metrics group; it is not itself a separately listed company. james cameron's first avatar film helped bring motion capture to a broad public audience and into mainstream production workflows. to achieve real-time visualization and rendering, the production built an entire virtual-production pipeline. its success won several academy awards and helped foster a number of well-known companies providing visual-effects workflow technology. noitom was founded in 2012 and introduced its first-generation product in 2014. we adopted a highly disruptive pricing strategy, reducing the cost by roughly two orders of magnitude. motion-capture work that previously required more than a million yuan could be done for tens of thousands. this quickly attracted users worldwide. our equipment has been used widely. starting with season five of game of thrones, for example, group characters such as the white walkers used our motion-capture equipment. more than ten systems on set allowed seven or eight stunt performers to capture all the movements. our equipment also participated in visual-effects production for wolverine, star trek, star wars and other projects. in sports, the coaching teams of golfers such as tiger woods and rory mcilroy have long used our equipment to analyze posture and the kinetic chain of the swing. several chinese olympic champions and the national modern-pentathlon team also use our system for digital analysis in routine training. our motion-capture technology is also used in virtual reality, games and interaction devices. companies including oculus, htc and sony playstation vr have used our technology licenses, services or accessories for hand tracking, digital gloves and vr interaction. in late 2023, we noticed a new source of growth in robotics. that prompted me to return my attention to the field and found noitom robotics to serve it specifically, working extensively with researchers and robot manufacturers. looking back, more than a decade of accumulated experience seems to have prepared us for this moment: combining human motion capture with intelligent robot control. it is meaningful work, and i feel fortunate to be doing it. motion capture is the process of digitizing human movement and pose. it is not limited to one technology: computer vision, sensors, magnetic tracking and exoskeletons can all do it. the core is recording and capturing poses and movements, then converting them into digital sequences. optical motion capture has long been considered a gold standard in research because it offers absolute spatial accuracy. here “absolute” refers to calibrated coordinates in the capture space, not zero measurement error. multiple high-speed industrial cameras use infrared light in the 850–950-nanometer range with global-shutter exposure. all pixels are exposed simultaneously, avoiding the row-by-row timing of a rolling shutter and providing high synchronization accuracy. high-end optical cameras can capture 1,200 frames per second; conventional systems typically operate at 120–240 fps. for full coverage in a room of roughly fifteen square meters, one or two cameras per square meter are often needed. professional whole-body capture, as in hollywood production, might use twenty to thirty cameras in that space. in a larger area of one hundred square meters, even a sparse installation may require forty to fifty cameras, each costing tens of thousands or even more than a hundred thousand yuan. high-quality optical systems can reach submillimeter positional accuracy, and a rigid body formed by several markers can have orientation accuracy of 0.05 degrees. that is why researchers consider it a gold standard for precision. optical systems, however, require complex installation and expensive equipment. a complete system often costs four hundred thousand to five hundred thousand yuan. inertial motion capture offers clear advantages in adaptability and convenience. it needs no external infrastructure and can work indoors or outdoors: put on the equipment, perform a few calibrations and start collecting. the cost is also much lower. the drawback of inertial capture is its lack of absolute positional accuracy. it estimates motion and pose from wearable sensors measuring angular velocity, acceleration and magnetic fields, and integration introduces cumulative drift. positional accuracy is generally at the centimeter scale and is relative rather than optical-grade absolute accuracy. vendors can delay drift through algorithmic improvements, but inertial capture does not provide the same absolute accuracy as optical systems. in robotics, optical capture is usually chosen when high-precision ground-truth data is needed, such as the absolute position of a person or object. inertial capture is more common in teleoperation and other scenarios emphasizing flexible environments, ease of use and real-time response. a more advanced option is hybrid optical–inertial tracking. it combines optical accuracy with inertial continuity, maintaining stable data under occlusion. if one hand blocks the other, the optical system may lose its markers while inertial sensors continue supplying data. sensor fusion can preserve both accuracy and continuity. exoskeletons are another early form of motion capture. in the late 1970s and early 1980s, some research institutions used exoskeleton structures with encoders to track human movement. as robotics research expanded, more researchers returned to exoskeleton-based teleoperation and capture, continuing that earlier idea. magnetic motion capture is another option. some vendors use high-frequency weak magnetic fields and three-axis coils to estimate a sensor's position and orientation, tracking gloves and controllers. such technology was used by the us air force and in other industrial applications, and later appeared in consumer products from companies such as razer. overall, motion capture has evolved for more than half a century, from experimental research systems in the 1970s to film production, sports analysis, virtual reality and today's robotics and embodied intelligence. it has become an important bridge between human movement and the digital world. from a systematic perspective, we first need to distinguish the purpose of the data: are we pursuing visual plausibility, or task success and manipulation precision? if the goal is visual plausibility, video-derived data can be useful. ailing zeng, a young researcher i know, participated in a very large dataset collecting internet videos; the reference is at the end. such data can be entirely adequate visually, because projected keypoints are usually accurate from the camera's viewpoint. the problem is missing depth. monocular video cannot guarantee precision along the depth axis. only stereo cameras with a sufficiently wide baseline can provide some depth reference, in the account given here. editorial clarification: monocular methods can estimate depth using motion cues or learned priors; a single rgb view alone does not uniquely specify absolute depth without additional assumptions. the dataset linked in this article is miradata, a video dataset, rather than a directly measured 3d motion-capture dataset. if the aim is to produce model outputs or robot behavior that looks plausible—for example, dancing or boxing with a visual resemblance to a human video—motions extracted from monocular footage may meet that need. the goal is for the movement to look similar from the video's viewpoint. that is a comparatively lightweight application. but highly dynamic movement with physical plausibility demands greater spatial precision: the robot must balance, jump, follow a path that closes back on itself, or interact with its surroundings. projects such as unitree's avatar-style teleoperation and yanjie ze's twist series, linked in the references, describe their platforms as humanoid teleoperation systems for collecting real interaction data. in that setting, spatial precision matters and more specialized motion-capture equipment is needed. the choice of professional equipment then depends on the environment and the objective, with two broad cases. in a laboratory or factory, the space is controlled, the budget may be relatively generous and accuracy requirements can be extremely high—for example, collecting coordinated two-handed actions. i recommend optical capture in that case. it is suitable for an indoor installation, accurate and well synchronized, making it ideal for research and high-quality collection. an institution such as amazon's robotics laboratory building a high-precision experimental system should use optical or hybrid optical–inertial tracking. in a changing environment, such as outdoors or a temporary setup, rapid deployment, lower cost and flexibility matter more. inertial capture is then more suitable. outdoor teleoperation or operation in ordinary, uninstrumented environments is well matched to this approach. different settings and needs can lead to completely different optimal choices. optical, inertial, magnetic and exoskeleton capture each have a reason to exist. that is why all remain in use and continue developing. choosing a system requires weighing the specific scene and environment case by case. first, you do not necessarily have to choose our equipment or data. i am happy to discuss the options and offer fair advice, then let each team decide for itself. the industry is still very young, and we want more people to help solve the data problem together. data is unquestionably the biggest bottleneck. language models can collect text across the internet, and autonomous-driving companies can gather large volumes from real vehicles. robotics has not yet reached that scale. real-world data can be divided into several categories. ultimately, all are needed, and they must work together to provide enough coverage in both volume and quality. first, real-robot teleoperation data is extremely important. human-centered or synthetic data cannot fully express the robot's own embodiment. only physical robot data contains its actual sensing, actuation and configuration characteristics, including manufacturing differences between models. it is expensive, inflexible and difficult to transfer across embodiments, but i believe every robot model still needs at least several thousand hours of real teleoperation data. this is like the automotive industry collecting substantial new road-test data for each vehicle model. a robot's configuration or hardware changes also require new collection. real-robot teleoperation is therefore indispensable, but cost and efficiency constrain its scale. i see its main role as aligning a model with embodiment-specific characteristics, rather than supplying most of the skill-learning data. skills and regularities should primarily come from other sources. researchers and companies have increasingly turned to human-centered collection. directly recording human interaction and visual information provides rich examples for robot imitation and understanding. this includes the largely visual interaction data represented by projects such as ego4d, egodex, egopressure and project aria or aria 2. there is disagreement over what human-centered data means. some researchers emphasize in-the-wild collection to ensure freedom and diversity. but genuinely natural collection requires sacrificing some modalities, dimensions or precision. a complex, burdensome wearable system cannot readily enter homes, factories or care homes. some teams try to have everything—huge scale, rich modalities and high precision—and encounter contradictory requirements. human-centered data may therefore need its own layers. the upper layer is comparatively smaller, highly precise, multimodal data, potentially on the scale of one hundred thousand to one million hours, establishing a high-quality benchmark across modalities and dimensions. below it is a larger volume of in-the-wild data, with simpler wearables and lower precision requirements, aiming for broader scene coverage. below that is another crucial layer: synthetic and internet data. it can augment real-robot and human-centered data at large scale. simulation and synthetic environments expand the diversity of trajectories, goals, backgrounds and strategies, multiplying the data volume by hundreds of times. autonomous driving used this approach early on, extending real data through simulation to cover extreme situations. i do not start from the question of how to promote our equipment or datasets. i want the industry to work together on the data bottleneck. without a complete data system built collaboratively, progress will stall. larger-scale, more advanced data-driven approaches are needed to move robot intelligence forward. noitom robotics is not simply an equipment manufacturer, and we do not want to be only that. noitom's earlier business can in many respects be seen as equipment manufacturing, but noitom robotics is different. we want to address the industry's data problem in multiple ways, acting as a service provider and a dataset licensor as well. for a considerable time, i will use equipment to make friends rather than profit from selling it. i will provide it free to many researchers. for strong industry partners, we may offer it at cost or partly as a gift. the purpose is to let more people use the technology and advance research and applications. i will devote substantial effort and capital to building our own data factory, accumulating datasets of one hundred thousand or even one million hours. the aim is to lower costs across the industry. that may sound contradictory: why would a third-party data company make collection cheaper? my logic is that only large-scale data that can transfer across embodiments and be reused is worth accumulating. we will find effective ways to align our human-centered datasets with the different robot configurations used by partners and customers, then license the data to them. cross-embodiment mapping allows repeated licensing and reuse, substantially reducing duplicated investment and waste across the industry. for example, we recently reached a data-licensing agreement with a large company on the scale of tens of millions in value. the licensed price was even slightly below the cost of collection. but i also spent a long time persuading the company to give up complete exclusivity. that business model can make industry-wide data accumulation more efficient and sustainable. i believe this is the greatest value we can provide. we need reasonable revenue to sustain an r&d team of dozens to more than a hundred people and keep investing in technology. at the same time, reusable datasets let the whole industry obtain high-quality resources at far less than the cost of collecting them independently. that is my vision, and it will take time to put it into practice. i will focus on this over the next two or three years. robot manufacturers, model companies and investors interested in the direction are welcome to discuss it with me. i am confident we can find suitable ways to work together. our greatest need at present is people. we are urgently recruiting in three categories. first are product managers and project managers. we need people in both data and robotics, whether junior or experienced. anyone committed to this direction is welcome. second are algorithm specialists. our chief scientist, lei han, is recruiting researchers with experience in multimodal models, vla, reinforcement learning and data science. we have openings for young researchers, interns and full-time research scientists and hope to attract people who truly care about robotics algorithms and models. third are sensor and hardware specialists. we have accumulated hardware experience, but that is only a starting point. most motion-capture and tracking equipment on the market was designed for film effects or games, not robot data collection. yet the robot-data market is much larger than the film market and has higher equipment requirements. it needs new hardware designed for different environments: in the wild, in factories and in research labs. we are actively pursuing that direction and especially need hardware-planning and sensor expertise: magnetic-positioning specialists, imu specialists, optical-sensor experts, engineers who turn algorithms into products, firmware engineers and bsp, or board-support-package, engineers. if you have experience in these areas or want to find an opportunity in a promising field, we welcome you. let me also take this opportunity for a straightforward commercial pitch. if your company or institution does not need to do everything internally, we would be pleased to partner with you. companies such as tesla and figure pursue full vertical integration, sometimes even saying they want to build their own vr systems. that is admirable, but it does not suit every company. if you have a clear boundary around your core business and want a specialist team to handle important supporting work such as data collection or dataset preparation, we would welcome the collaboration. with the most reasonable pricing, the greatest enthusiasm and the highest professional standards, we can help you complete the work efficiently. references the twist series miradata, a lab 和 tencent robotics x 实验室。 早期我的研究方向主要是强化学习。那时候我们在做游戏 ai，尝试将强化学习应用到游戏场景中。那也是alphago 刚出现的几年，我们主要研究博弈论、复杂对弈类游戏的策略空间与动作空间，开发能够在复杂游戏中达到超越人类水平的智能体。 大约在 2019 年至 2020 年 期间，我转入腾讯的机器人实验室，开始从事机器人运动控制相关研究。那个阶段整个行业的硬件还没有现在这么成熟，所以我们实验室也在做自研硬件，包括自制机器人平台和四足机器人。在这些自研平台上，我们将强化学习和模仿学习等算法技术结合，用于机器人控制与运动规划。 一直到今年上半年，我们观察到整个行业的发展速度显著加快。尤其是在具身智能领域，对数据的质量与多模态多样性的需求变得越来越迫切。我们意识到，未来机器人智能能力提升的核心瓶颈之一，不仅在算法，而在于如何获取和管理高质量的数据。 正因为如此，我和戴博士（戴若犁）一起创办了诺亦腾机器人（noitom robotics），希望能在高质量多模态数据采集与具身智能训练体系方面，探索并构建行业级的技术基础设施。 其实我最早接触强化学习是在 2015 到 2016 年左右。那时 alphago 刚出来，对我冲击很大。我第一次真切感受到，有一种算法能够在没有明确数据集的情况下，仅凭“胜负”这样极简的 0/1 信号，就能学出超出人类经验的数据分布之外的策略。那时候我就对强化学习特别痴迷，也因此一路坚持做相关研究。到现在我仍然相信，rl 是实现 human-level 甚至 superhuman 智能的一条必要技术路径。 不过，随着研究问题越来越复杂，尤其是进入真实世界和机器人领域后，我也越来越清楚，仅靠纯粹的 rl 是不够的。就像大语言模型一样，智能体要想在复杂环境中高效学习，必须先通过大规模数据训练积累大量“预备知识”，这样 rl 才能在其基础上更高效地迭代。这一点其实在游戏 ai 阶段我们就已经体会到了。 以围棋为例，2015、2016 年时大家认为围棋是极其复杂的游戏，但 alphazero 证明，通过纯强化学习的自博弈（self-play）也能解决它。回头看，这其实说明了围棋的 action space 仍然较小。但当问题升级到像 rts 这种即时战略类游戏时，就不能再用 alphazero 那样“从零开始”的方式。必须先通过人类专家数据或 replay 学到一个不错的 warm start 基础模型，再用 rl 继续优化。这样探索空间的效率会成倍提升，最终策略也会更优秀。 从 2020 年开始，我们就尝试把机器人与 ai、尤其是强化学习结合起来。那时我们开始使用一些仿真系统，把机器人放进模拟环境里训练，就像在玩一个“物理游戏”。我们当时的想法很直接：能不能像做 game ai 那样来做机器人控制？ 在仿真环境里，这种方式确实很快能学到不错的结果。比如 2018 年 jason peng（专访xue bin(jason) peng：探索人形机器人全身运控的通用控制器）的基于强化学习的人体动作控制技术路线是非常值得尊敬的工作，能够在虚拟环境里让角色模仿人类动作，对后续的虚拟角色和机器人控制有很大的影响力。但当我们进一步把模型从仿真转移到真实物理世界时，就发现问题远比想象复杂。 当时我们自己在做机器人硬件开发，因为那时市面上还没有太多成熟的消费级平台，所以我们一边摸硬件、一边摸算法，也体会到这两者的融合是一个需要长期迭代的过程。仿真训练很容易出成果，但要真正让机器人在现实中稳定执行，就会遇到很大的落差。这也让强化学习在机器人领域的挑战从“如何设计复杂策略空间”，变成了“如何解决 sim2real gap”。 游戏是一个完全定义好的理想环境，训练和测试条件一致；但真实世界的物理环境充满不确定性。于是，这几年行业内出现了很多尝试，比如通过域随机化（domain randomization）来让仿真环境覆盖尽可能多的真实物理变化。这是一种有效的路径，但它的代价很高——随机化会让模型花大量时间去探索一些现实中根本不会遇到的情况。只有覆盖足够多的随机情境，模型才有可能在真实世界里工作。这种方法提升了鲁棒性，但大大降低了训练效率。 强化学习的核心问题在于探索效率。做游戏 ai 时我们就知道，如果完全从零开始学习，效率非常低。更高效的方式是先让模型聚焦在几个比较优秀的初始解上，再在此基础上继续做小范围的探索，这样效率会高得多。 当然，提前用监督学习去做 warm start 也会带来另一类问题——可能会限制最终策略空间，让模型陷入局部最优。但总体来看，一个更好的路径是：先训练出一个好的基础模型（base model）或初始策略，再接入强化学习去做微调和策略优化。这样不仅效率更高，也能在复杂的机器人系统中更稳健地实现持续提升。 我可以讲一下为什么觉得数据非常重要。按照我们前面讨论的思路继续往下推，如果想真正达到 human level 的智能水平，不需要达到 super human 的程度，就会发现这是一个越来越复杂的大模型或者 agent 的问题，也就是机器人的问题，它的整个空间都会变得越来越大，而高质量的数据是支撑这一切的核心。 当时我也做过一段时间的大语言模型，那个时候我看到大语言模型训练数据的体量和机器人相比，差距非常大，完全不是一个量级。因为语言模型的语料来源于互联网、twitter、博客等，每天新增的文本数据量远远超过目前所有机器人领域汇总起来的全部数据量。那时我就意识到，只有当数据体量达到类似的规模，才有可能为机器人或 agent 的基础模型提供最基本的能力，更不用说在这个基础上再去做 sft 或强化学习。 从整体来看，机器人领域确实发展很快，硬件在不断迭代，ai 算法在运动控制、基础操作等方面也能展现不错的结果，能让大家看到一些令人满意的 demo。但是从数据体量和第一性原则的角度来看，机器人的问题要比大语言模型复杂得多。机器人涉及的模态更多，不只是文本，还包括视频、图像、触觉以及其他模态，整个空间更大、更复杂。而现在机器人可用的数据量却比文本数据小得多。那时我就意识到，如果未来要真正解决机器人的关键问题，数据一定是核心，但目前现有的数据收集方式仍然存在问题。 过去主流的技术路线vla主要是用遥操真机数据，大家普遍采用的方式是使用遥控器、手柄、主从臂或动捕系统，通过人来遥控机器人采集真机数据，最早包括pi0等，整个领域内的主流数据收集方式都是这样。我们自己也做过大量这样的尝试，收集了很多遥操真机数据。在这个过程中，我们发现数据收集效率很低。人操控机器人时，操作方式并不符合人的自然习惯，需要扭头观察机器人的本体，有时因为遮挡看不清，还要调整姿势。整个过程中没有触觉反馈，视觉反馈也是间接的。效率非常低，比如一个人几秒钟就能完成的桌面操作，用机器人执行可能需要几十秒甚至一分钟以上。 第二个问题是，收集数据必须绑定具体的硬件本体。虽然不同本体之间的数据可能有一定的泛化能力，但我们做过实验，用混合不同本体的数据进行训练，发现更多的泛化仍停留在视觉理解阶段。而在真正执行层面，这些数据往往难以复用，甚至可能出现某一构型的数据会影响另一构型的执行能力。这样一来，数据收集既受效率限制，又受本体约束，要在规模上继续扩展非常困难。 继续思考后，我们看到 vla 往后的发展方向可能有两条路。一种是通过遥操数据训练出一个基础模型，然后在真实机器人上接入强化学习，这是一条合理的技术路径，比如dyna在做类似的事。另一种思路是使用更多模态的数据来解决问题。那回顾过去，我们在做locomotion的时候，不会像 vla这样依赖遥操数据。训练locomotion研究者往往采用强化学习的方法，在仿真环境中进行大量随机化训练，从而让机器人学会运动控制。这条路径与 rl 结合得非常紧密，研究者会用动捕数据或视频数据进行模仿学习，从中抽取信息训练模型。 回到前面的问题。首先，数据是最重要的。高质量的数据能让机器人更接近真实本体，更高效地实现真机 demo。但要想进一步扩大数据规模，如果不想继续绑定硬件本体去收集数据，那么下一个可能的方式就是基于人类数据（human data）。这类数据的体量至少可以比之前高出一到两个数量级。 因为这类数据直接来自人类，不再绑定具体机器人本体，可以形成统一的数据格式。虽然每个采集者的体型不同，但他们都是人类，基本结构一致，不需要再考虑机器人自由度、关节或单独部件参数的差异。这样的人体数据格式更统一、更具泛化性。 我也知道动捕设备的成本较高，但诺亦腾机器人在该领域已有约十几年的经验，在批量部署和数据收集方面积累丰富，效率很高。我本人以前作为诺亦腾的客户，也采购过他们的光惯混合动捕设备，体验不错，所以我认为这件事完全可行。 现在我们将 human-centric 数据作为第二条主要技术路线。我们会在一个类似“动捕笼子”的环境中，尽可能使用惯性和光学结合的动捕系统。采集者佩戴轻便的追踪器，物体上安装小型光学标记，同时利用 rgb-d 第三视角相机、激光雷达等多模态传感器，采集人类动作、物体交互以及环境的三维模型。这类数据模态非常丰富。我们还会在采集者的手上配备柔性触觉手套，不影响操作习惯的情况下记录触觉信号。最终，我们得到的是一个以 human-centric 视角为核心的多模态数据体系。 与遥操真机数据相比，这种方法不再过度依赖机器人本体，数据规模可以扩展到原来的数十倍甚至上百倍。另一个优势是精度高，这套动捕系统中，人的手指与物体的空间贴合误差可以小于 1 毫米，达到亚毫米级精度。第三个优势是模态丰富，能够完整记录视觉、触觉、运动等信息。 当然，这样的技术路线也带来额外的挑战。首先需要解决的是重定向（retargeting）问题。由于数据不再依附具体机器人本体，必须能将人类动作映射到不同机器人构型上。解决方式包括强化学习，通过模仿学习后再强化探索；也可以直接学习一个神经网络模型，把人类动作数据当作一种特定构型的机器人进行vla的预训练，实现跨本体的训练。这样，人类就可以被视为统一的“机器人本体”。 除此之外，这类数据在其他领域也有广泛应用。例如在世界模型（world model）、三维视频生成、三维场景生成等研究中，它都能发挥作用。因为它完整记录了人类与环境交互的多模态信息，适用范围极广。 虽然这类 human-centric 数据模态丰富，但仍受限于可控环境。通常需要在实验室或封闭空间中搭建这样的采集系统，无法达到互联网级别的体量。因此，我们还在探索第三层数据模态——轻便型可穿戴设备数据。人可以佩戴手表、眼镜或帽子等装置，在不影响日常生活的情况下采集数据。这类设备能更贴近真实生活场景地记录人机交互，同时我们也会重视隐私与合规问题。 未来的进一步发展，可能是使用互联网中的第三视角视频，例如 youtube、twitter 等平台的视频数据，构建类似互联网文本那样的 internet-scale 数据体系。 我们认为数据大体可以分为四层，从上到下形成一个金字塔结构。越往下，数据体量越大，模态越多，但与真实机器人本体的距离也越远。不同层的数据各有侧重和不足。 对于诺亦腾机器人而言，我们希望能整合不同模态、不同层级的数据，为整个行业提供高质量的数据基础，服务于各种技术路线。无论未来 ai 模型的发展方向如何变化，这些数据模态都能为不同路线提供支持。我们希望能把整个数据模态体系准备好，方便行业内的团队在此基础上探索多样化的 ai 模型路径。这正是我们正在做的事情。 这是一个非常关键的问题。先回答第一个问题，关于诺亦腾机器人是否会关注视频相关的数据，答案是肯定的。我们在采集以 human-centric 为主的数据时，一个非常重要的部分就是会使用头戴式设备，获取第一人称视角下的 ego-centric video 数据。 这类视频数据的特点是从人的视角出发，与互联网常见的第三视角视频或自由拍摄（freestyle）的视觉风格不同。它真正关注的是人眼前的操作场景，比如双手正在执行的动作，或者行走时看到的视野范围。我们会重点收集这些与操作和具身行为密切相关的第一视角视频数据。 此外，我们还会在视频基础上同步采集深度信息或鱼眼信息，以获得更广角、更完整的视觉输入。这些信息都是我们在视频数据采集中会重点获取的内容。 回到第二个问题，确实，计算机视觉（cv）的发展速度非常快。未来如果视频数据的处理做到足够好，它完全有可能在世界模型（world model）中实现对物理世界的重构与高精度预测。 但这里存在一个第一性原理层面的限制——信息维度的问题。简单来说，从二维视频中去估计三维信息，本身是信息缺失的。除非有多个视角，否则仅依靠单一 2d rgb 画面很难精准还原 3d 信息。举个例子，人如果闭上一只眼，只用单眼去看，会发现双手手指对齐都会出现误差，这说明单一视角无法完整捕捉空间深度信息。 因此，仅依靠二维视频数据无法提供精确的三维信息。视觉发展的方向，应该是结合多模态数据，通过将 2d 视频与 3d 结构化数据融合，为世界模型提供高质量输入，从而更准确地预测和重建三维世界。从原理上来说，信息的完整性决定了模型的能力。只有当视觉模型融合了多模态数据，包含足够丰富的三维物理世界信息，才能真正具备精准重建世界的能力。 或许在未来，human-centric 的视频数据最重要的使用方向之一，不仅仅是具身智能，也可能是服务于世界模型或计算机视觉模型。无论最终被用于哪个方向，它们的前提都是这些数据本身提供了最基础、最关键的模态信息来源。 5. 怎么看缺乏3d信息的世界模型 现在已经有一些非常优秀的研究工作在探索类似的方向。前一段时间，英伟达发布了名为 cosmos 的世界模型，随后他们的团队以及其他研究者也陆续推出了一系列相关研究，其中有一个名为 dreamgen 的项目给我的启发特别大。 dreamgen 的核心思路，是利用一个基于视频生成的世界模型，在虚拟环境中不断进行推演。它生成的画面是机器人在操作场景中的动作过程，模型能够提前预测接下来的画面帧。研究人员会从这些生成的视频中提取出动作信息，再用这些数据去训练机器人行为策略。 这个思路非常典型：希望通过世界模型生成大量视频，让模型自己在“想象”的环境中学会一套行为规律。但从实验结果来看，这种方式的准确率仍然比直接用遥操作数据训练要低。这是可以理解的，因为它缺乏机器人在真实物理环境中与物体接触时的一些关键细节，例如三维空间的位置坐标、关节的姿态与速度等物理信息。 它的优势在于，可以显著提升多样性和泛化能力，因为模型可以在想象中模拟出各种不同的场景和动作。但它的不足在于，缺乏真实世界中精确的末端执行数据，也就是在实际动作执行阶段的物理精度。 这些工作非常有探索意义。随着研究的深入，人们会发现不同技术路线各有侧重：有的更注重多样性和想象能力，有的更关注精准控制。当未来真正出现能够同时包含三维物理信息的世界模型时，这条技术路线也会变得完全可行。前提仍然是要有足够大规模、足够高质量的数据集来支撑，这一点又回到了最核心的数据问题。 这是一个非常实际的问题。获取动捕数据的成本确实很高，而这也是当前许多实验室普遍面临的困难。针对这一点，动捕技术本身已经非常成熟，可以支持大规模、高效率的数据采集。近期的目标，是为整个社区提供数百小时到上千小时规模的高质量动作捕捉数据集。这将成为行业内少有的、覆盖范围广且精度高的大型数据资源。 作为对比，目前常见的数据集amass规模大多只有几十个小时，lafan的体量还会更低。正因为现有动捕数据普遍较少，研究者往往不得不从视频中提取动作信息来补充。从视频中抽取动作数据的方式虽然方便，用普通相机或手机即可完成，但在精度上存在明显的局限。相比之下，大规模、高精度的动捕数据能够在数据质量和可靠性上带来质的提升。 诺亦腾机器人计划提供的数据集将在体量上达到现有水平的数十倍甚至百倍，为研究人员和开发者提供足够丰富的高质量动捕数据。这项工作正在积极推进中。目前的一些数据集中会出现动作悬空、侧滑等问题，行走类动作占比较高，而高动态动作的比例偏低。这正是当前重点改进的方向之一。 在数据质量方面，已经进行了大量投入。通过在模型训练中不断验证和打磨数据，持续提升其精度与稳定性。目标不仅是提供数量充足的数据，更要确保其质量达到研究与应用的标准。在对数据进行充分利用和验证后，将以研究者的标准确保数据的高质量与可用性，再在此基础上扩大规模，为更多使用者提供可靠的数据资源。 8. 诺亦腾机器人动捕数据采集的优势 诺亦腾在动捕设备领域已有十余年的技术积累，在设备技术细节、采集成本控制以及大规模数据采集的运营能力方面，具备显著优势。这套系统的灵活性也非常高。诺亦腾采用的是光学与惯性相结合的混合式动捕技术，这是目前全球范围内极少数能够实现高精度与高连续性兼顾的方案。 纯光学动捕的优点是精度高，但在遇到遮挡或高动态动作时容易出现丢帧；惯性动捕虽然能保持连续性，但在位置精度上会存在偏差。通过将两种技术融合，系统能够在保证高精度的同时维持连续性，避免丢帧问题。这套高质量的捕捉硬件设备和数据融合算法是其中的核心技术。 此外，在动捕数据采集过程中，还可以灵活组合多种感知模态。采集人员在进行动作捕捉的同时，可佩戴其他传感设备，例如头戴式视觉系统或手部触觉传感器，从而同步采集视觉、触觉等多模态信息。这种多模态组合的方式，使得数据在模态丰富度、采集精度以及整体效率方面都能保持较高水准。这正是目前最具优势、最擅长开展的工作方向之一。 9. 动捕+rl在解决操作任务上的机会 我认为这件事情一定会有机会，而且操作任务真正能够落地时，强化学习这一环节是必不可少的。这始终是一条值得坚持的技术路线。 现在，无论使用哪种类型的数据，大家基本都能先训练出一个效果还不错的基础模型。接下来要怎么做，就变得非常关键。有一部分技术路线选择直接在真实机器人上进行强化学习，也就是在人参与的情况下完成整个训练过程。这种方式通常针对特定任务进行优化，可以把某些任务的成功率提高到九成以上。比如在叠衣服这样的案例中，就采用了强化学习的方式，通过设置评估函数来不断迭代策略。 这种方法的优势很明显，但问题在于需要大量人力参与整个训练过程。无论从人力投入还是规模化角度来看，成本都非常高，挑战也很大。 另一种做法与运动控制相似，在仿真环境中进行反复训练。仿真的好处是可以不受限制地探索，代价只是算力。这种方法同样有机会，但也存在自己的难点。运动控制的问题相对简单，因为即使地形复杂，环境本身也是静态的，只有机器人在其中运动，机器人的参数与仿真模型也能做到非常接近，所以训练出来的策略偏差很小。 而操作任务则不同，它需要与可移动、带有物理属性的物体交互。碰撞会成为一个很大的问题。因为操作过程中不只是面对静止不动的物体，还需要与会移动、具备动力学特性的物体打交道，这种接触和动态变化发生的概率非常高，所以在仿真中进行操作类强化学习时难度更大，sim2real gap也更高。 还有一些研究正在探索新的方式。例如，有团队直接使用以人为中心的数据，比如动捕数据，不直接做强化学习，而是选取人手动作中的关键点，将其映射到机器人手部的对应关键点上。然后把机器人的遥操作数据与动捕数据结合，一边是人的手，一边是机器人的手，先建立两者的对应关系，再把这两类数据合并进行联合训练。 通过这种方式，可以把人类的动作数据融入操作策略中，经过联合训练后，动捕数据能够融合进模型的策略部分。这样不仅能引入大量人类动作数据，还能在此基础上形成一个具备基础能力的模型，为后续的强化学习提供起点。 这是目前能够看到、并且非常值得探索的一些方向，尤其是在操作场景中，都是未来可能进一步发展的技术路径。 reference： https://www.leihan.org/ an interview with lei han: noitom robotics and the human-data challenge, part one lei han discusses reinforcement learning, the human-data pyramid, optical–inertial motion capture, multimodal collection and opportunities for robot manipulation. in the human data series conclusion, human data—the key to robot data, we summarized the human-data pyramid. for the first of our closing interviews, i am delighted to speak with lei han, chief scientist of noitom robotics, a company working on data challenges at different levels of that pyramid. longtime smart note readers may remember my 2023 article, a map of chinese researchers in ai and robotics. for the final two interviews in the human data series, i had the privilege of an in-depth conversation with one of the researchers featured in that map: lei han. at the time of this interview, lei han was cofounder and chief scientist of noitom robotics. previously, he spent six years at tencent's robotics x laboratory as director of embodied intelligence and principal research scientist. before that, he was a senior research scientist at tencent ai lab. before joining tencent, lei was an assistant research professor in the department of basic science at mississippi state university in the united states. he received his phd from peking university, advised by professor kunqing xie, and subsequently conducted postdoctoral research at hong kong baptist university with professor yu zhang and at rutgers university with professor tong zhang. his research interests include large-scale statistical machine learning, reinforcement learning, optimization and multi-task learning, and their applications in robotics, games, natural language processing, computer vision and bioinformatics. before this formal interview, i had asked lei on several occasions about combining reinforcement learning with robotics. i greatly appreciate the depth and breadth of his technical thinking. in this conversation, i asked him about robot data, particularly human data, as well as current algorithmic approaches in robotics. i strongly recommend listening to or reading the discussion. search for respark on xiaoyuzhou to listen to the podcast. podcast: conversation with lei han: reinforcement learning and motion-capture data—noitom robotics' data story, part one. listen in the original wechat article. contents ↓ 1. introduction 2. reinforcement learning's development across fields 3. why start a company focused on robot data? 4. will motion capture still matter if video data makes a breakthrough? 5. the importance of 3d information for video data 6. contributions to the research community 7. comparing motion-capture approaches 8. opportunities for motion capture plus rl in manipulation i am chief scientist and cofounder of noitom robotics. before founding the company, i spent eight years at tencent, working first at tencent ai lab and then at tencent robotics x. my early research focused mainly on reinforcement learning. we were developing game ai and trying to apply rl to games. this was in the years around alphago's emergence. we studied game theory and the strategy and action spaces of complex competitive games, developing agents that could surpass human performance. around 2019–2020, i moved to tencent's robotics laboratory and began researching robot motion control. hardware across the industry was less mature than it is now, so the lab also developed its own hardware, including custom robot platforms and quadrupeds. on these platforms, we combined reinforcement learning, imitation learning and other algorithms for robot control and motion planning. by the first half of 2025, the year of this interview, we could see the industry's development accelerating significantly. in embodied intelligence, the demand for high-quality, diverse multimodal data was becoming especially urgent. we realized that a core bottleneck in improving robot intelligence was not just algorithms, but how to acquire and manage high-quality data. that is why ruoli dai and i founded noitom robotics. we hope to explore and build industry-level technical infrastructure for high-quality multimodal data collection and embodied-intelligence training. i first encountered reinforcement learning around 2015–2016. alphago had just emerged, and it had a profound impact on me. for the first time, i felt that an algorithm could learn strategies beyond the distribution of human experience, driven by a minimal zero-or-one signal such as winning or losing, without relying on a predefined dataset in the same way as supervised learning. i became fascinated with rl and have continued researching it ever since. i still believe it is a necessary technical path toward human-level or even superhuman intelligence. editorial clarification: alphago itself used human game data as well as rl; the purely self-play, from-scratch approach discussed below was demonstrated later by alphazero. as the research problems became more complex, especially in the real world and robotics, i also became increasingly aware that pure rl is not enough. as with large language models, an agent learning efficiently in a complex environment must first accumulate substantial preparatory knowledge through large-scale data training. rl can then iterate more efficiently on that foundation. we had already learned this during our game-ai work. take go. in 2015–2016, it was considered an extremely complex game, yet alphazero later showed that pure reinforcement learning through self-play could solve it. looking back, that suggests go's action space is still relatively small. once the problem becomes something like a real-time strategy game, we cannot simply begin from scratch in the alphazero manner. we need human expert data or replays to obtain a good warm-start base model, then use rl to optimize it further. that greatly improves exploration efficiency and produces a better final strategy. from 2020 onward, we tried combining robotics with ai, particularly reinforcement learning. we used simulators to train robots, almost as if they were playing a physics game. our thinking was straightforward: could we approach robot control in the same way we approached game ai? in simulation, this can indeed produce good results quickly. xue bin (jason) peng's 2018 work on reinforcement learning for human-motion control, for example, is a highly respected research direction. it allows virtual characters to imitate human movements and has had a major influence on subsequent virtual-character and robot control. see interview with xue bin (jason) peng: exploring a general controller for whole-body humanoid control. but transferring these models from simulation to the physical world revealed problems much more complex than we had expected. we were developing our own robot hardware because there were not yet many mature consumer-level platforms available. exploring hardware and algorithms together showed us that integrating them requires long-term iteration. simulation training produces results relatively easily, but making a robot execute reliably in reality exposes a large gap. the central rl challenge in robotics therefore shifted from designing complex strategy spaces to addressing the sim-to-real gap. a game is a fully specified, idealized environment, with consistent training and testing conditions. real physical environments are full of uncertainty. the industry has explored approaches such as domain randomization, making simulation cover as many real-world physical variations as possible. it is effective, but expensive: the model spends a great deal of time exploring situations it may never encounter in reality. only after covering enough randomized scenarios may it work reliably on a real robot. this improves robustness but greatly reduces training efficiency. exploration efficiency is a core problem in reinforcement learning. we knew from game ai that learning entirely from scratch is inefficient. it is much more effective to begin with a few promising initial solutions and explore a smaller region around them. of course, supervised warm-start training introduces another risk: it may restrict the eventual strategy space and trap the model in a local optimum. overall, however, i think the better route is to train a strong base model or initial policy first, then use rl for fine-tuning and policy optimization. this is more efficient and supports more robust, continuous improvement in complex robotic systems. let me explain why i think data is so important. following the reasoning we discussed, even reaching human-level intelligence—without aiming for superhuman performance—becomes an increasingly complex large-model or agent problem. robotics is such a problem. its overall space keeps expanding, and high-quality data is the foundation supporting all of it. i also spent some time working on large language models. the gap between the volume of language-model training data and robot data was enormous: they were not even on the same scale. language models draw on the internet, twitter, blogs and other sources. the new text generated each day far exceeds all the robot data currently collected together. that made me realize that robot or agent foundation models can only acquire even their most basic capabilities once the data reaches a comparable scale before we even consider subsequent supervised fine-tuning (sft) or reinforcement learning. robotics is developing rapidly. hardware continues to improve, and ai algorithms can already deliver good results in motion control and basic manipulation, producing impressive demos. but from the perspective of data volume and first principles, robotics is much more complex than language modeling. it involves more modalities—not just text, but video, images, touch and others—and a larger, more complex space. yet the available robot data is far smaller than the text corpus. i realized that data would be central to solving robotics' key problems, while existing collection methods still had limitations. the mainstream vla approach has mainly used teleoperated real-robot data. people use remotes, handheld controllers, leader–follower arms or motion-capture systems to operate a robot and collect physical demonstrations. early models such as π0 and much of the field followed this approach. we collected a great deal of teleoperation data ourselves and found it inefficient. operating a robot does not match natural human habits. you need to turn your head to inspect the robot, sometimes adjust your posture because of occlusions, and work without tactile feedback and with only indirect visual feedback. a tabletop task that takes a person a few seconds may take the robot tens of seconds or more than a minute. second, data collection is tied to a specific hardware embodiment. data may generalize somewhat between embodiments, but our mixed-embodiment training experiments found that much of the transfer occurred at the visual-understanding level. at execution, the data was often difficult to reuse. data from one configuration could even impair another configuration's execution. with both efficiency and embodiment constraints, further scaling becomes very difficult. we then saw two possible directions beyond the current vla approach. one is to train a base model from teleoperation data and then apply reinforcement learning on the real robot. that is a reasonable technical route; dyna, for example, is pursuing something along those lines. the other is to use a wider range of data modalities. looking back at locomotion, we did not rely on teleoperation data in the same way as vla. researchers often use rl with extensive randomization in simulation to teach motion control. this route is closely integrated with rl, while motion-capture or video data provides imitation references and information for training. returning to the earlier question: data is the most important factor. high-quality data brings a model closer to the actual embodiment and makes real-robot demonstrations more efficient to achieve. to expand the data volume without continuing to tie collection to robot hardware, the next possibility is human data. its volume could be at least one or two orders of magnitude larger. because it comes directly from people, this data is no longer tied to a particular robot embodiment and can use a unified format. people differ in body shape, but they share the same basic structure. we do not need to account for robot-specific differences in degrees of freedom, joints or individual component parameters. human data can therefore have a more consistent format and greater generality. i know motion-capture equipment is expensive, but the noitom team has more than a decade of experience in the field, including efficient large-scale deployment and data collection. i previously bought its hybrid optical–inertial motion-capture equipment as a customer and had a good experience. that makes me confident this approach is feasible. we now treat human-centered data as our second major technical route. in a motion-capture enclosure, we use a combination of inertial and optical tracking wherever possible. participants wear lightweight trackers, and objects carry small optical markers. rgb-d third-person cameras, lidar and other sensors capture human movement, object interaction and 3d models of the environment. the resulting modalities are rich. we also equip participants with flexible tactile gloves that record touch without disrupting their normal manipulation habits. the result is a multimodal data system centered on human activity. compared with real-robot teleoperation, this approach is much less dependent on the robot embodiment. data volume can potentially expand by tens or even hundreds of times. another advantage is precision: in our motion-capture system, the spatial alignment error between a person's fingers and an object can be less than one millimeter, reaching submillimeter accuracy. a third advantage is the richness of modalities, recording visual, tactile and motion information together. this route also creates challenges. the first is retargeting. since the data no longer belongs to a specific robot embodiment, we must map human movements to different robot configurations. one approach combines imitation with further reinforcement learning and exploration. another directly learns a neural model, treating human motion data as if it came from one particular robot configuration during vla pretraining and enabling cross-embodiment training. in that sense, the human body becomes a unified robot embodiment. this data also has applications beyond robot policy learning, including world models, 3d video generation and 3d scene generation. it records multimodal information about human interaction with the environment, giving it a very broad range of uses. although human-centered capture provides rich modalities, it remains constrained by a controlled environment. such a collection system typically needs a laboratory or enclosed space and cannot reach internet scale. we are therefore exploring a third data layer: lightweight wearables. people could wear watches, glasses, hats or other devices to collect data without disrupting daily life. these devices record human–machine interactions in settings closer to everyday reality. privacy and compliance are also important considerations for us. a further direction is to use third-person videos from platforms such as youtube or twitter, building an internet-scale data system comparable in reach to internet text. we divide data into roughly four layers, forming a pyramid from top to bottom. moving downward, the volume grows, the range of modalities broadens and the distance from the actual robot embodiment increases. each layer has its own strengths and limitations. editorial clarification: the modality mix depends on the collection method; not every lower layer contains every higher layer's sensor measurements. at noitom robotics, we want to integrate data across modalities and levels, providing a high-quality data foundation for the industry and supporting different technical approaches. whatever direction ai models take, these modalities can support multiple routes. we hope to prepare the overall data system so that teams can explore different model approaches on top of it. that is what we are working on. that is a crucial question. first, will noitom robotics work on video-related data? absolutely. an important component of our human-centered collection is head-worn equipment that captures first-person, or egocentric, video. this video comes from a person's viewpoint, unlike the third-person or casually filmed footage commonly found online. it focuses on the scene directly in front of the person: what their hands are doing, or what they see while walking. we will prioritize this first-person video closely connected with manipulation and embodied behavior. we also capture synchronized depth information or fisheye imagery, obtaining a wider and more complete visual input. these are important components of our video-data collection. on the second question, computer vision is indeed progressing very rapidly. if video processing becomes good enough, it may enable world models to reconstruct the physical world and make highly accurate predictions. there is nevertheless a first-principles limitation: the dimensionality of the information. estimating 3d information from 2d video involves missing information. without multiple viewpoints, a single rgb view makes precise 3d recovery difficult. for example, close one eye and try to align your fingertips. you may notice errors, illustrating that one viewpoint does not capture all spatial-depth information. therefore, 2d video alone cannot provide precise 3d information. vision should combine modalities, integrating 2d video with structured 3d data to give world models high-quality inputs for more accurate prediction and reconstruction. information completeness constrains a model's capability. only visual models that fuse multimodal data containing sufficiently rich information about the 3d physical world can truly reconstruct it precisely. editorial clarification: this is han’s argument for explicit physical information; monocular methods can estimate 3d structure using learned priors and motion cues, but a single rgb image does not uniquely determine absolute geometry without additional assumptions. in the future, one of the most important uses of human-centered video may extend beyond embodied intelligence to world models or computer-vision models. whatever the application, the premise is that the data supplies fundamental, essential information across modalities. 5. world models without 3d information there is already excellent research exploring related directions. nvidia recently released its cosmos world models, followed by related work from its team and other researchers. one project that particularly inspired me is dreamgen. dreamgen's central idea is to use a video-generating world model to roll out robot behavior in an imagined environment. it generates frames showing a robot acting in a manipulation scene and predicts what comes next. researchers then extract action information from the generated videos and use this data to train robot behavior policies. it illustrates a common idea: generate large quantities of video with a world model and use these imagined environments to learn behavioral regularities. judging from the experimental results, however, this approach’s accuracy remains below that of training directly on teleoperation data, in my assessment. that is understandable, because the generated video lacks some critical details of real physical contact, such as precise 3d coordinates, joint configurations and velocities. editorial clarification: the interview discusses a precision trade-off; this is not a claim that synthetic data never improves a real-data baseline. its strength is greater diversity and generalization, because the model can imagine different scenes and actions. its weakness is the lack of precise real-world execution data, particularly at the end effector during physical action. these projects are valuable explorations. as research advances, we will see different routes emphasize different things: some prioritize diversity and imagination; others prioritize precise control. a future world model that also contains 3d physical information could make this route fully viable. it still needs sufficiently large, high-quality datasets. that brings us back to the fundamental data problem. this is a very practical issue. motion-capture data is expensive to obtain, and many laboratories face that difficulty. yet the capture technology itself is mature and supports large-scale, efficient collection. our near-term goal is to provide the community with hundreds to more than a thousand hours of high-quality motion-capture data. that would be an unusually large resource with broad coverage and high precision. for comparison, established datasets such as amass have motion data on the scale of tens of hours, and lafan is smaller still in the comparison we are discussing. because existing motion-capture datasets are limited, researchers often extract motions from videos to supplement them. that is convenient—a normal camera or phone is enough—but has clear precision limits. large-scale, high-precision motion capture could substantially improve data quality and reliability. the dataset noitom robotics plans to provide aims to be tens or even hundreds of times larger than existing resources, offering researchers and developers abundant high-quality motion-capture data. work is actively underway. some current datasets contain floating or foot-sliding artifacts, include a high proportion of walking, and have too little highly dynamic movement. those are among the issues we are trying to improve. we have invested heavily in data quality, repeatedly testing and refining the data through model training to improve accuracy and stability. the aim is not merely to provide enough data, but to meet standards for research and application. after thoroughly using and validating it, we will assess its quality and usability from a researcher's perspective, then scale it further to provide a reliable resource for more users. 7. noitom robotics’ advantages in motion-capture data collection (section 8 in the original numbering) noitom has more than a decade of technical experience in motion-capture equipment. it has substantial strengths in equipment details, cost control and operating large-scale collection. the system is also flexible. noitom uses hybrid optical–inertial motion capture, one of the relatively few approaches worldwide that can combine high accuracy with continuous tracking. pure optical capture is accurate but can lose frames during occlusion or highly dynamic movements. inertial capture maintains continuity but can have positional errors. combining them allows the system to maintain both accuracy and continuity while avoiding tracking dropouts. the high-quality capture hardware and sensor-fusion algorithms are the core technologies. during motion collection, we can also combine sensing modalities flexibly. participants can wear additional equipment, such as head-mounted vision systems or tactile sensors on their hands, to record visual and touch information synchronously. this multimodal combination supports rich modalities, precise capture and high overall efficiency. it is one of our strongest areas of expertise. 8. opportunities for motion capture plus rl in manipulation (section 9 in the original numbering) i believe there is definitely an opportunity here, and reinforcement learning will be essential when manipulation tasks become practically deployable. it remains a technical route worth pursuing. whatever data type they use, teams can generally begin by training a reasonably capable base model. what happens next is crucial. some approaches apply rl directly on real robots, with people participating throughout training. this usually optimizes a specific task and can raise its success rate above 90%. clothes folding, for example, has used rl with an evaluation function to improve the policy iteratively. the advantages are clear, but substantial human involvement is needed throughout training. both the labor cost and the challenge of scaling are considerable. another approach resembles locomotion research: train repeatedly in simulation. simulation allows unrestricted exploration, with computing as the main cost. this is promising too, but has its own difficulties. motion control is relatively simple because even on complex terrain, the environment is often static and only the robot moves through it. the robot's parameters and simulation model can also be made quite close, so the trained policy's mismatch can be small. manipulation is different. it requires interaction with movable objects that have their own physical properties. collisions become a major issue. the robot is not merely facing stationary objects; it must handle moving objects and their dynamics. contacts and dynamic changes occur frequently, making rl for manipulation in simulation harder and increasing the sim-to-real gap. other research explores alternative routes. some teams use human-centered data, such as motion capture, without applying rl directly. they select keypoints from human hand motions and map them to corresponding robot-hand keypoints. they then combine robot teleoperation data with motion-capture data: establish correspondences between the human and robot hands, then merge the two sources for joint training. this brings human motion into the manipulation policy. through joint training, motion-capture data becomes part of the policy model. it introduces substantial human-motion data and yields a model with basic capabilities that can serve as a starting point for later reinforcement learning. these are promising directions already visible today, particularly for manipulation, and they are technical routes worth exploring further. references

传统的retargeting方法，机器人重定向后的动作里会出现一些不太自然的表现，还经常发生穿模。omniretarget的效果整体看起来更自然，而且能够很好地保持交互，并真正落实各种硬约束。此外omniretarget还可以进行数据增强，减少对原始动捕数据数量的依赖，而之前那些 retargeting 的方法其实很难做到这一点。 这篇访谈来自对omniretarget一作之一杨麓洁的专访，麓洁博士毕业于mit，师从russ tedrake教授，本科毕业于加州大学伯克利分校，师从 francesco borrelli 教授。她的研究方向是将机器学习、优化和控制理论结合起来，用于机器人系统的规划与控制。开发同时利用数据驱动与模型驱动优化的方法，使机器人在灵巧操作、复杂接触等任务中具备更高的性能和可靠性。
